newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares close lower on EMU worries.
newsitem.headline: German shares close lower on EMU worries.

text.p: German shares turned sharply lower after a strong start on Monday, as an upsurge in worries about European monetary union offset initial optimism about U.S. economic prospects.
Sheer vertigo was another factor behind the downturn, traders said, as the thinly-traded market simply failed to sustain the record highs achieved in early trade.

The blue chip DAX index closed the floor session down 27.86 points, or 0.8 percent, at 3,667.43 points -- dropping nearly 70 points from the historic intraday high of 3,734.05 points set in pre-bourse electronic dealings.
Despite a strong start to Wall Street, the IBIS DAX index of all-day electronic trade did not manage to recoup any of the losses, with it ending at barely above bourse levels at 3,668.61.

The main spur for the decline was a comment from newly-elected French finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn, who said he could not yet agree on the stability pact designed to ensure fiscal discipline under monetary union.

The dollar slid sharply on the news, always a negative for German exporters, and confidence was further hurt by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel's dogged insistence on strict fulfilment of Maastricht budget goals -- a scenario widely viewed as impossible for cash-strapped Germany.
"This all raises the question - how is the euro going to be achieved?" said one dealer.
"One thing is sure, if people really start to worry about this, there will be chaos in the markets," he added.
Thomas Mayer, senior economist at Goldman Sachs in Frankfurt, said however that markets were overreacting.
"I think the French are playing for time," he said.

"It would have been far more surprising if a new French government, just a week old and at its very first internationally-significant meeting, were to simply have followed in the footsteps of their predecessors."
Early trading saw a rally and new record highs on the market amid relief at reassuring economic news from the U.S. which had sent Wall Street powering to record levels on Friday.
But German prices started to fall off their highs as follow-up orders failed to materialise and the dearth of strong corporate news took its toll.

The few outperformers of the day included Karstadt AG, which ended bourse trade up 1.20 marks at 621.20 marks, having hit an early high of 636 marks, after a story that the WCM group was planning to buy a 25 percent stake in the retailer resurfaced in the Handelsblatt daily newspaper.

WCM later denied this. Deutsche Bank AG, one of the banks reported in the German media to be ready to sell a stake in Karstadt, declined comment while Commerzbank AG reiterated that it was not aware of any such a plan.
